html:
The Jaru are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southeast Kimberley in Western Australia, around present-day Halls Creek. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language is still spoken.

Their neighbours were the Kija to the north, the Gooniyandi and Walmajarri to the west and the Ngarti to the east. In 1885 gold was found at Halls Creek, the first gold rush in Western Australia. Thousands of miners crossed Jaru land for a few years, and cattle stations followed. Many Jaru later worked on those stations.
